search-penalty.context: A search result page with a heavy arrow pointing down and a gavel beside it. Used for ranking drops after a search engine penalty, manual actions and SEO sanction reports.

seo-cloaking.context: A page with a theatre mask over its upper half and a robot and a person shown below. Marks cloaking, where a site shows search bots different content than visitors, in SEO audits and spam policy pages.

alt-text.context: An image frame with a mountain and sun above two lines of caption text. Used for alternative text fields on images, accessibility checks and media library descriptions.

aria-label.context: A button shape with a small luggage-style tag tied to its corner by a string. Stands for ARIA labels and accessible names given to controls for screen readers.

contrast-ratio.context: An outlined square overlapped by a solid square, with a colon of two dots beside them. Used for colour contrast checkers and WCAG contrast ratio readings such as 4.5:1.

keyboard-navigation.context: A keycap with a tab arrow inside, surrounded by four focus brackets. Used for keyboard-only navigation, tab order testing and visible focus indicator settings.

dyslexic-font.context: The letters b and a with heavy bars under them on a baseline. Used for dyslexia-friendly font toggles and reading-aid settings that switch to a weighted typeface.

reduced-motion.context: Three horizontal speed lines beside a circle holding a pause symbol. Used for reduce motion preferences, animation off switches and settings for people sensitive to movement.

colorblind-mode.context: An eye whose iris is split into a solid half and an outlined half. Used for colour blindness modes, colour-safe palette switches and vision accessibility settings.

semantic-html.context: A page outline split by lines into a header bar, a side navigation strip, a main area and a footer bar. Used for HTML landmark elements, document structure and markup tutorials.

switch-access.context: A large dome push button on a flat base with a cable running off to the side. Used for switch access devices that let people with limited movement control a computer with one or two buttons.

screen-magnifier.context: A monitor with a magnifying glass ring over a letter on the screen. Used for screen zoom tools, low vision settings and magnification features.

accessibility-audit.context: A clipboard holding a small standing figure with arms out. Used for accessibility audit reports, WCAG conformance reviews and inclusive design checklists.

readability-score.context: A page with two text lines and a half-circle gauge with a needle at the bottom. Used for readability analysers and reading grade scores in writing and SEO tools.

focus-trap.context: A dialog box with a circular arrow cycling inside it. Used for modal focus management, where keyboard focus loops within an open dialog until it closes.

braille-display.context: A flat bar with raised dot cells across the top and a row of small keys along its front edge. Used for refreshable braille displays and tools for blind computer users.

eye-gaze-control.context: An eye with a dotted line running from its pupil down to a pointer on a monitor. Used for eye tracking input, gaze-controlled computing and hands-free access tools.

audio-captcha.context: A verification box with an empty checkbox, a speaker and a sound wave. Used for the audio option of CAPTCHA challenges for people who cannot read distorted images.

web-vitals.context: Three small round gauges with needles at different angles. Used for Core Web Vitals reports covering loading, interactivity and visual stability scores.

layout-shift.context: A solid content block with a dashed ghost copy below it and a downward arrow. Used for cumulative layout shift warnings where page content jumps while loading.

lazy-loading.context: A page with a solid mountain image at the top and dashed empty placeholder boxes below it. Used for images and content that load only as the visitor scrolls near them.

code-splitting.context: Three separate rectangular code blocks with gaps between them, each holding short lines. Used for splitting JavaScript bundles into chunks that load on demand.

tree-shaking.context: A small tree with round leaves drifting away from its crown. Used for removing unused code from JavaScript bundles during the build.

page-hydration.context: A browser window with a water drop falling onto the page. Used for hydration, where server-rendered HTML becomes interactive in the browser.

performance-budget.context: A wallet with a clasp tab and a small speed gauge on its front. Used for web performance budgets that cap page weight, script size and load time.

http-compression.context: A narrow file page squeezed between two vertical jaws with arrows pushing inward. Used for gzip and Brotli response compression settings on servers and CDNs.

image-compression.context: A large image frame with an arrow pointing to a smaller image frame. Used for image optimisation tools that reduce file size, such as WebP converters.

page-cache.context: A page standing inside an open box next to a small lightning bolt. Used for page caching plugins and fast stored copies of rendered pages.

render-blocking-script.context: A script block with angle brackets standing across the bottom of a browser window like a barrier. Used for performance audits that flag scripts holding up the first paint.

bundle-size.context: A parcel box sitting on a small weighing scale. Used for bundle analysers and reports on how heavy JavaScript and CSS packages are.

dropped-frames.context: A film strip with a solid frame on each side and a dashed empty frame between them. Used for frame rate monitors and reports of animation jank and stutter.

container-query.context: An outer box holding a smaller component and a short ruler line along its inner top edge. Used for CSS container queries, where a component adapts to its parent width.

content-management-system.context: A browser window with stacked content blocks and a pencil standing beside it. Used for CMS admin areas where editors write and publish page content.

headless-cms.context: A stack of content blocks sending three arrows out to a watch, a monitor and a phone. Used for headless CMS platforms that serve one content source to many devices through an API.

block-editor.context: Three stacked content blocks with a round plus button beside the middle one. Used for block-based page editors where authors add blocks one at a time.

page-builder.context: A browser window with a dashed target slot and a pointer dragging a section block toward it. Used for drag-and-drop website builders and landing page editors.

content-calendar.context: A calendar grid with small post bars placed on several days under two binder rings. Used for editorial calendars and social media publishing schedules.

user-roles.context: Three people in a row, the middle one taller and wearing a small crown. Used for user role and permission settings such as admin, editor and subscriber.

website-theme.context: A browser window with a paint palette on the page. Used for theme pickers, template galleries and site appearance settings.

comment-moderation.context: A speech bubble with a short text line and a small gavel at its lower corner. Used for comment approval queues, spam review and community moderation tools.

static-site-generator.context: A gear beside a page stack, with a lightning bolt on the front page. Used for static site builders that generate plain pages ahead of time.

featured-image.context: A post page with a framed image marked by a star above a short line of text. Used for choosing the main image of a blog post or article.

multisite-network.context: A browser window at the top linked by lines to three smaller windows below. Used for multisite networks where one install runs many websites.

code-playground.context: A browser window split into a left code pane with an angle bracket and a right preview pane. Used for live code editors where markup and its result appear side by side.

z-pattern-layout.context: A page outline with a bold Z path running from the top left to the bottom right. Used for the Z-pattern reading flow in landing page and layout design.

f-pattern-layout.context: A page outline with an F-shaped set of scan lines along its top and left side. Used for the F-pattern reading behaviour seen in text-heavy page design.

asymmetric-layout.context: A page split into a wide left column holding blocks and a narrow right column with a single line. Used for uneven two-column designs and editorial page layouts.

broken-grid-layout.context: A grid of rounded blocks where one tall block breaks out of its row. Used for overlapping, offset and experimental web layouts that break a strict grid.

map-list-layout.context: A screen split into a list of three rows on the left and a map with a pin on the right. Used for store locators, property search and any page that pairs listings with a map.

product-listing-layout.context: A page with a narrow column of checkboxes beside a two by two grid of product cards. Used for shop category pages with filters and a product grid.

client-logo-strip.context: A horizontal band holding a row of four plain shapes: a circle, a square, a triangle and a hexagon. Used for trusted-by sections that show customer or partner logos.

feature-grid.context: A three by two grid of small squares, each with a short line beneath it. Used for features and benefits sections on landing pages.

visual-hierarchy.context: Three stacked bars that shrink in size and weight from the top to the bottom. Used for typographic hierarchy, heading levels and content priority in design guides.

above-the-fold.context: A page with a dashed horizontal line across its middle and content filled in above it. Used for the above-the-fold area, the part of a page visible without scrolling.

long-scroll-page.context: A tall page passing behind a corner-bracket screen frame, with a two-way arrow at its side. Used for long scrolling pages, one-page sites and scroll depth settings.

shape-divider.context: A page with two sections separated by a wavy edge. Used for curved and wave section dividers on landing pages.

lightbox-gallery.context: A framed enlarged picture in the centre with small arrow chevrons on both sides. Used for photo galleries that open images in an overlay with next and previous controls.

fluid-layout.context: A page with content blocks and a small outward arrow at each side. Used for fluid, percentage-based layouts that stretch with the window width.

mobile-first.context: A large phone outline standing in front of a smaller monitor outline. Used for mobile-first design strategies where small screens are planned before large ones.

browser-viewport.context: A browser window with dashed corner brackets marking the visible area inside it. Used for viewport size settings, screenshot area pickers and responsive testing tools.

neumorphism.context: A rounded square raised from the page, with a light edge at the top left and a shadow edge at the bottom right. Used for the soft UI style with embossed buttons and gentle shadows.

lorem-ipsum.context: A dashed frame holding three lines of wavy placeholder text. Used for dummy copy generators and text placeholders in layout mockups.

css-box-model.context: Four nested rectangles, each smaller one centred inside the one before. Used for the CSS box model showing margin, border, padding and content.

author-box.context: A box with a round portrait on the left and a name line with two bio lines on the right. Used for the author bio under blog posts and articles.

related-posts.context: Two lines of article text above a row of three small cards. Used for related article blocks that suggest more reading under a post.

social-share-bar.context: A vertical strip of four small circles attached to the left edge of a page. Used for sticky share buttons that float beside an article.

zigzag-sections.context: A page with three rows where the image block alternates between the left and right of the text. Used for alternating feature rows on landing pages.

fullscreen-menu-overlay.context: A window covered by a panel with three long menu lines and a small close cross at the top right. Used for full-screen navigation menus opened from a hamburger button.

full-bleed-image.context: A page with text lines above an image band that runs to both page edges. Used for edge-to-edge images that break out of the text column.

scroll-reveal.context: A page whose blocks change from solid to outlined to dashed going down, with a downward arrow at its side. Used for scroll-triggered fade-in effects.

web-design.context: A browser window with a pen nib on the page and a ruler line at its right. Used for website design services, design tool sections and creative portfolios.

usability-testing.context: A person at a monitor with an eye above the screen. Used for usability studies where researchers watch how people use a site or app.

design-handoff.context: An artboard frame with a bent arrow leading down to code angle brackets. Used for passing finished designs to developers for building.

cross-browser-testing.context: Three overlapping browser windows with a tick in the front one. Used for compatibility checks that confirm a site works in several browsers.

fieldset.context: A rectangle border whose top edge is broken by a short label bar, with two input lines inside. Used for grouped form fields with a legend.

input-mask.context: An input field showing a pattern of short dashes and underline marks. Used for formatted entry such as phone, card and date fields.

terms-checkbox.context: A ticked checkbox beside a small document with a folded corner. Used for agree-to-terms boxes on sign-up and checkout forms.

form-submissions.context: An inbox tray holding a sheet with short lines standing in it. Used for lists of received form entries and lead inboxes.

site-health.context: A browser window with a heartbeat pulse line across the page. Used for website health checks, uptime monitors and site status dashboards.
